fresh_checks.check: The closed trace functional is positive on nonzero pseudoeffective classes and bounds finite-dimensional norm on the compact unit-sphere slice; nef approximations give the stated closed cone.

Perturbed minimal multiplicities are independent of the fixed Hermitian background. Zero perturbed multiplicities characterize nefness by regularization, without requiring every representative to have zero poles.
Finite intersections use maxima followed by regularization with an explicit positivity margin. The local quadratic replacement excludes isolated poles while retaining strict positivity.

The Demailly–Păun class-C implication and Collins–Tosatti null-locus identification retain their cited hypotheses and recorded external scopes. This read does not independently certify the source papers.
The Hopf zero-class example has infinite perturbed Hermitian upper mass at fixed epsilon. The finite class-C invariant uses closed Kähler forms on resolutions instead.
Each resolved subspace is in class C. The common graph refinement and closed pullback comparison identify the restricted invariant without choosing an ambient Kähler metric.
Closed positivity bounds the mass of C+t kappa by its cohomological integral, uniformly over representatives. The same closed control is unavailable for arbitrary nonclosed perturbations.
Modification descent and the absence of non-pluripolar mass on analytic sets justify the mass pushforward. No pullback of an arbitrary measure is introduced.
The closed positive-mass/bigness implication uses the cited BEGZ input. Nef zero mass and positive mass are distinguished before identifying numerical loci.

In the normalized diagonal construction the coefficient retained in the first-factor pushforward is positive when L kappa-b is positive. The cited Demailly–Păun concentration input keeps its original scope.
The Hermitian comparison form controls the pushforward current; the local product calculation uses closed Kähler forms. Rank drop annihilates the indicated top wedge.
The union includes positive-dimensional subspaces inside the exceptional locus; the positive dimension restriction and actual restricted mass are retained.
The bounded residual is removed on a common resolution. Its positivity implication gives nefness; the resulting polynomial coefficients are closed mixed intersections.
Divisor metric changes cancel in the residual current. Ordinary-equivalent analytic types have identical divisor coefficients on a common refinement.
A strict representative gives only the stated one-sided trace estimate. The blowup obstruction shows that strict positivity need not preserve the original bounded type.
The hyperplane restriction has mass d^k while the ambient polynomial is (c+d)^k. In the projective threefold blowup the exceptional squared trace is zero while the indicated sectional trace is one.
The inequality c<=b(1-kappa)^n retains kappa in [0,1). Weak trace annihilation and attainment by a uniformly integrable selecting family are different conclusions.
The exposed face uses the closure of smooth positive Gauduchon tests. A negative-self-intersection divisor current supplies the obstruction to arbitrary positive-current smoothing.
The determinant vanishes on the positive-rank locus. The root measure is supported on the stated degeneracy set, and a positive prescribed density there is excluded in the claimed regime.
The zero root pairing is necessary under nefness. No general converse or arbitrary-regularity assertion is derived.
The positive top coefficient is zero for every L1 damping input in the Hopf model, despite positive lower Hermitian volume. This does not imply bounded mass.
The vertical mass vanishes. Matrix positivity eliminates mixed terms, and the distributional fiber-constant argument gives descent of the closed positive current.
Harmonic fiber integration gives the indicated injection. The two-dimensional cone example does not describe the entire Bott–Chern group; the trace normalization is 8 pi.
Ordinary and ideal product envelopes have the stated zero top mass. Truncation does not recover ambient closed positivity.
The exact selected-space and norm pushforward has intrinsic growth degree two; ambient degree-three normalization erases its limit.
The volume 24 pi epsilon(a+epsilon)(b+epsilon) has order 3-q in the stated cases. It is the background volume for the chosen family, not conserved mass of a fixed density.
The displayed Omega_epsilon square is dd^c-closed; the integral is 8 pi. The coefficient and root-denominator limits distinguish q=0,1,2.
The rank-two square cannot be a finite root in the indicated degeneration. The denominator epsilon^(q/3) does not by itself prove concentration of the prescribed measure.
The global Lp density, minimal type and strict analytic barrier apply on the entire fixed open regular locus. A density smooth only on a smaller punctured set does not meet that assertion.
The ramification divisor provides the global barrier for the finite map. Coordinate-power Hopf maps descend and give positive nonclosed backgrounds with zero closed top mass.
The determinant and tangential trace bounds yield an all-path minimum-eigenvalue lower bound. The radial endpoint model is stated with its separate G_a control.
The completed-square identity uses conjugate transpose and the positive Schur complement. The path equation is solved within nested coordinate neighborhoods.
A smooth metric coefficient along exceptional vertical directions is O(|z|^2). The codimension r-1 density condition is necessary only.
The local determinant is constant, but the compactly glued density has only the specified global Lp range p<n/(n-1). It does not satisfy the full fixed-locus smoothness hypotheses.
Monotone m(s) permits positive gluing. The determinant and blowup Jacobian give ell=n gamma-1; normal distance has order gamma and Lp integrability requires p ell>-1.
The ell=0 and ell=n models retain the stated smooth-density/Hessian distinction. Outer nonclosed perturbation is allowed only in its described support.
The exact mass equation m(s)^n=n integral_0^s t^(n-1)D(t)dt gives the radial eigenvalues m/s and m-prime. The prescribed tail matches the Fubini–Study background.
The extension is atomless with zero Lelong number. Exact full-mass closed uniqueness applies to this data; unbounded zero-Lelong solutions need not have minimal type.
The radial length integral sqrt(m-prime)/(2 sqrt(s)) controls every path from below and a radial path from above. Divergence gives completeness of the punctured compact locus.
The complex Jacobian contributes |z|^(2(n-1)). The pullback is an isometry off the exceptional divisor and preserves the stated extended equation.
For D asymptotic to C s^(n(gamma-1))L^(-b), the constant K=(C/gamma)^(1/n) and potential tail K s^gamma L^(-b/n)/gamma are consistent with the exact mass equation.
Finite mass requires b>1; boundedness and finite distance both require b>n+1. The equality potential has the log-log divergence, and none of these singular densities lies in Lp for p>1.
For the iterated-log model finite mass holds for every fixed real d. Boundedness requires d>n, finite distance d>2n; n<d<=2n gives bounded continuous complete non-Hölder potentials.
The normalized mean-one curve density solves the global Poisson equation. Atomlessness and the vanishing of two curve factors give the exact extended product measure.
The potential C0 r^(2(tau+1))/(tau+1)^2 has Hessian C0 r^(2 tau), zero boundary flux, and finite normal distance for tau>-1. For tau=-a the Lp threshold is pa<1.
P_b double-prime=4 C0 t^(-b), including the b=2 branch. Finite mass requires b>1, and boundedness/finite distance require b>2.
For 1<b<=2 the potential has zero Lelong number and trivial multiplier ideals but is unbounded. Closed full-mass uniqueness excludes a different bounded solution for the same normalized data.
The incidence section has bundle pi^*O(1) tensor q^*O(-1). Poincaré–Lelong gives T=beta+2[E] for theta=3 beta-2 gamma and rho=2 log s.
The 5/2 logarithmic barrier gives (beta+gamma)/2+5[E]/2. The exceptional degree -2 prevents nefness.
The quotient beta^2/s has the displayed smooth strictly positive blowup-chart density. The exponential right side cancels to beta^2 off E and is extended by zero on E.
Isolated puncture extension on the projective plane gives u<=rho+C for every theta-psh potential. Bounded difference from V_theta and finite closed mixed masses give finite relative energy.

fresh_checks.topic: exponential uniqueness with infinite raw weight
fresh_checks.check: The unweighted s^(-1)dV measure has infinite mass, while the two weighted Monge–Ampère integrals are finite. Closed comparison forces equality without assuming finite raw mass.

fresh_checks.topic: ample locus and every open subset
fresh_checks.check: Every potential has a pole on E, while the strict current is smooth off E. Each connected open subset is isometric to a proper projective-plane open set and has a finite-length first-exit Cauchy path.
The example concerns a big non-nef class. Completeness in nef classes and under geometric-flow compatibility remains open.
The ratio det_omega T/det_omega B_tau is the intrinsic Schur complement. The finite divisor cover gives |partial tau|^2 comparable to R^(-2), including dimension one.
The normal inequality gives the proper Lipschitz function integral x^(-p/2)dx when p<=2. Bounded Cauchy sequences remain in a compact regular subset and converge.
The density, lower potential and upper tangential determinant yield exponent p=q+a+b. Integrability q>1 and the upper bound for global quasi-psh potentials give finite right-hand mass.
The two cutoff logarithmic profiles have vanishing distributional boundary terms. A common large C ensures positivity, and the exact curve-product measure gives full background mass, including n=1.
For 0<lambda A<1 the density is integrable, with q=2-lambda A, a=lambda A, b=0. The intrinsic normal criterion proves completeness for all paths.
The bounded profile has integrable density, minimal type and full mass, but the explicit normal path has finite length. Its exponent is 2+beta for every beta>0.
F=R^2 f tends to zero in the logarithmic examples; it is not claimed smooth positive across the divisor. The prescribed nonintegrable-pole and flow questions remain unsettled.
